The alpha channel is squeezed into the first feature channel, where alpha equals one when the first feature channel is non-zero and zero otherwise [S2].

The claim states that the alpha channel is squeezed into the first feature channel, where alpha equals one when the first feature channel is non-zero and zero otherwise. Source [S2] explicitly states: 'To avoid having an extra image to store the binary alpha (opacity) channel, we squeeze the alpha channel into the first feature channel, so that the alpha is one when the first feature channel is non-zero, and zero when the channel is zero.' This matches the claim exactly.

Texture Image Storage allocates 8-dimensional features across two 4-channel PNG images, totaling 8 channels [S2].

The claim states that Texture Image Storage allocates 8-dimensional features across two 4-channel PNG images, totaling 8 channels. Source [S2] explicitly confirms this in section F: 'Since the features to be stored are 8-dimensional, we use two PNG images to store them. Each PNG image has 4 channels, therefore two PNG images have a total of 8 channels to store 8-d features.' All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.

Large texture images are split into multiple 4096×4096 images to satisfy mobile hardware constraints requiring power-of-two dimensions capped at 4096×4096 [S2].

The claim states that large texture images are split into multiple 4096x4096 images to satisfy mobile hardware constraints requiring power-of-two dimensions capped at 4096x4096. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Since phones have a hardware constraint that the texture size must be a power of 2 and at most 4096 × 4096, we split the large texture images into multiple 4096 × 4096 texture images.' This matches the claim exactly.
